## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

1	// Agent invocation (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §12, §14.6). The executor starts the
2	// agent session with an API CALL rather than by arming a label event, which is
3	// what retires the re-arm, the grace window and the transport dance — and what
4	// makes a lost hand-off a synchronous, visible failure at the executor instead of
5	// a label event fired into the void.
6	//
7	// A TASK NAMES AN ENDPOINT, NEVER A URL. The declaration is vendored verbatim
8	// into every consuming repo, so it must never carry deployment detail or anything
9	// adjacent to a credential: `invocation_endpoint: 'fleet'` names a key, and the
10	// repo's own config maps that key to a URL and to the NAME of the repo Actions
11	// secret holding its token. That indirection is also what replaces the whole
12	// self/fleet apparatus — reach is a property of which endpoint you call, so a
13	// task needing wider access names a different endpoint and nothing else in the
14	// system needs a concept of scope.
15	//
16	// THE PROMPT NAMES ONE ITEM AND CARRIES NO INSTRUCTIONS. Everything
17	// behavior-defining is read by the session from the tracked task files at HEAD;
18	// the prompt says which issue and which nonce, and the session validates both in
19	// code before acting (DESIGN §7).
20	
21	export const DEFAULT_ENDPOINT = 'default';
22	
23	// The endpoint is a ROUTINE'S API TRIGGER — `POST /v1/claude_code/routines/
24	// <trigger-id>/fire` with a per-routine bearer token — which is what Claude Code
25	// on the web actually exposes to an HTTP caller. Three consequences the design's
26	// "a CCR API call" did not spell out, each verified against the routines docs
27	// rather than assumed:
28	//
29	//  - THE BEHAVIOR IS THE ROUTINE'S STORED PROMPT, not ours. `text` reaches the
30	//    session wrapped in a `<routine-fire-payload>` block explicitly labelled
31	//    untrusted, and a routine acts on it only because its own saved prompt says
32	//    to. That is the issue-is-data posture arriving for free at one more hop: our
33	//    payload names an item, and every instruction comes from a stored artifact.
34	//    The routine's stored prompt is one line pointing at `instructions.md` beside
35	//    this file, so the whole of what a session does is tracked and reviewed.
36	//  - THE BODY CARRIES ONE FIELD. `text` is freeform and unparsed — structured
37	//    JSON would arrive as a literal string — so the item number and nonce go in
38	//    as prose, and nothing else goes in at all.
39	//  - THERE IS NO IDEMPOTENCY KEY (standing entry 11, answered: the endpoint
40	//    offers none), which is exactly why THIS MODULE CALLS ONCE PER ITEM AND NEVER
41	//    RETRIES. A retry is only safe when you know the first call did nothing, and
42	//    a client-side timeout is the one case where you cannot know — the session
43	//    may well have started. Retrying there is what would make invocation
44	//    at-least-once and put two sessions on one item; declining to retry is what
45	//    keeps it at-most-once and lets the whole agent-side claim protocol delete.
46	//    An outcome we did not learn is reported as UNKNOWN and resolved by the agent
47	//    leash, which is a rule that already exists, rather than by a guess here.
48	//
49	// The beta header is dated and the endpoint is a research preview whose two most
50	// recent header versions keep working, so it lives in config with a default here
51	// — a rotation is then a config edit on one repo, never an engine release the
52	// whole fleet waits for.
53	export const DEFAULT_HEADERS = Object.freeze({
54	  'anthropic-beta': 'experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01',
55	  'anthropic-version': '2023-06-01',
56	});
57	
58	// The endpoint a task's hand-off calls, resolved against the repo's config.
59	// Returns `{ name, url, tokenEnv, headers }` or `{ name, error }` — a task naming
60	// an endpoint the repo has not configured is a repo-configuration fact, reported
61	// where the operator reads it, never a crash.
62	export function resolveEndpoint(config, task) {
63	  const name = task?.decl?.invocation_endpoint ?? DEFAULT_ENDPOINT;
64	  const endpoints = config?.taskScheduler?.endpoints ?? {};
65	  const entry = endpoints[name];
66	  if (!entry) {
67	    return { name, error: `this repo's config declares no invocation endpoint "${name}" (taskScheduler.endpoints)` };
68	  }
69	  if (!entry.url) return { name, error: `invocation endpoint "${name}" declares no url` };
70	  if (!entry.tokenSecret) return { name, error: `invocation endpoint "${name}" declares no tokenSecret (the NAME of the repo Actions secret holding its token)` };
71	  return { name, url: entry.url, tokenEnv: entry.tokenSecret, headers: { ...DEFAULT_HEADERS, ...(entry.headers ?? {}) } };
72	}
73	
74	// The fire payload: which item, and the nonce that proves this call is the one
75	// the hand-off comment recorded. Prose, not JSON — the field is freeform and
76	// unparsed, so a structured payload would arrive as a literal string — and
77	// deliberately free of instructions, because the routine's stored prompt is what
78	// says how to act on it (see `instructions.md`). The session still validates
79	// the item in code before touching it: a payload labelled untrusted is trusted no
80	// more than a label event was.
81	export const firePayload = ({ repo, item, nonce }) =>
82	  `Claudinite work item: ${repo}#${item.number}. Invocation nonce: ${nonce}.`;
83	
84	// The invoker seam the executor calls, exactly once per item. Failure is DATA,
85	// never a throw, and it comes in two kinds the caller must treat differently:
86	//
87	//   { ok: true, sessionId, sessionUrl }   the routine fired; a session exists
88	//   { ok: false, answered: true, error }  the endpoint ANSWERED and refused —
89	//                                         no session, and the cause is a
90	//                                         configuration fault a retry cannot fix
91	//   { ok: false, answered: false, error } no answer reached us — a timeout, a
92	//                                         dropped connection. The session may or
93	//                                         may not exist, and nothing here may
94	//                                         guess which.
95	export function agentInvoker({ repo, config, env = process.env, fetchImpl = fetch, timeoutMs = 60e3 }) {
96	  return async function invoke({ task, item, nonce }) {
97	    const endpoint = resolveEndpoint(config, task);
98	    // A configuration fault, decided before any call: definite, and no session.
99	    if (endpoint.error) return { ok: false, answered: true, error: endpoint.error };
100	    const token = env[endpoint.tokenEnv];
101	    if (!token) {
102	      // The `required_secrets` posture, applied to the endpoint token: nothing
103	      // fails silently, the task just doesn't work yet, and the item names which
104	      // secret to set (DESIGN §14.7).
105	      return { ok: false, answered: true, error: `the Actions secret \`${endpoint.tokenEnv}\` for invocation endpoint "${endpoint.name}" is not set in this repo` };
106	    }
107	
108	    const payload = { text: firePayload({ repo, item, nonce }) };
109	
110	    // ONE call. No loop, and deliberately no `attempts` knob for anyone to raise.
111	    try {
112	      const res = await fetchImpl(endpoint.url, {
113	        method: 'POST',
114	        headers: {
115	          ...endpoint.headers,
116	          'content-type': 'application/json',
117	          authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
118	          'user-agent': 'claudinite-executor',
119	        },
120	        body: JSON.stringify(payload),
121	        signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs),
122	      });
123	      let json = null;
124	      try { json = await res.json(); } catch { json = null; }
125	      if (res.status >= 200 && res.status < 300) {
126	        return {
127	          ok: true,
128	          sessionId: json?.claude_code_session_id ?? null,
129	          sessionUrl: json?.claude_code_session_url ?? null,
130	        };
131	      }
132	      // A status came back, so the endpoint decided: no session was started, and
133	      // the cause is a token, a URL or a routine — none of which a retry fixes.
134	      return {
135	        ok: false, answered: true,
136	        error: `endpoint "${endpoint.name}" returned ${res.status}${json?.error ? `: ${JSON.stringify(json.error)}` : ''}`,
137	      };
138	    } catch (e) {
139	      // Nothing came back. The request may have landed and started a session, so
140	      // this is the one outcome that must never be retried and never be reported
141	      // as a failure — it is genuinely unknown, and the caller says so on the item.
142	      return { ok: false, answered: false, error: `endpoint "${endpoint.name}" gave no answer: ${e.message}` };
143	    }
144	  };
145	}

1	# Update — the apply stage
2	
3	The deterministic half already ran. Preprocessing converged this repo's mount to the
4	canon's current engine and pack versions, ran the version-ranged migrations, gated the
5	result on the converged tree's own `selftest --strict`, and opened the update PR. The
6	dispatch issue names the branch and says which packs moved.
7	
8	**You are here for one of two reasons**, and the issue says which:
9	
10	- **Withheld workflow files** — content the deterministic half already decided but its
11	  Action token is refused for. Nothing here needs judgment; you are the credential.
12	- **A pack's updated rules have met content this repo authored** and the canon has never
13	  seen. This is the half that needs judgment, and it is all of the judgment there is.
14	
15	## 1. Read why you are here
16	
17	The dispatch issue's **Why the agent is here** section names the terminal and the packs
18	whose versions moved. That is binding scope — do not widen it.
19	
20	## 2. Deliver any withheld workflow files
21	
22	GitHub never lets an Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` write under `.github/workflows/`, and the
23	refusal rejects the whole push — so the update flow stages that content instead of
24	committing it where it belongs. Anything staged is already on the branch, already in the
25	PR's diff, and already correct.
26	
27	If `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` has files in it, then for each one:
28	
29	- Move it to `.github/workflows/` under the same name — **byte for byte**.
30	- Delete the staged copy.
31	
32	Do not reformat it, do not reorder it, do not reconcile it against what the file used to
33	say. It is a converged artifact, not a draft: the cron minute is a hash of this repo's
34	full name and the `env:` block is the union of every scheduled task's `required_secrets`,
35	so an "improvement" here silently changes when this repo runs or which secrets its tasks
36	can see. A staged file that looks wrong is a `needs-human` end (§5), reported with what
37	looked wrong — that is a canon bug, and editing it here would hide it while leaving every
38	other member broken.
39	
40	An empty or absent `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` means there is nothing owed. Do not
41	create it, and never move a file INTO it.
42	
43	## 3. Apply the new rules
44	
45	Only if the issue's reason names a migration record — it names them by path, e.g.
46	`packs/basics/migrations/2026-08-13-something`. **Read that record** at
47	`.claudinite/shared/<path>/migration.mjs`: its `applyStage.instructions` say what its
48	author wanted done, in their words, and are the specific half of this section. The
49	record is on the branch you were given because the update that raised it vendored it
50	there. A record the issue names but the branch does not carry is a `needs-human` end
51	(§5) — guessing at what its author wanted is worse than reporting it missing.
52	
53	Then, on that branch:
54	
55	- Bring this repo's own content in line with the updated pack rules, and repair the
56	  tests those rules break.
57	- Nothing outside that scope. No new features, no unrelated tidy-ups, no rewriting a
58	  member-authored local pack beyond what the new rules require.
59	
60	## 4. Verify the executor routine
61	
62	The one check no Action can make. This repo's executor routine fires on the
63	`ready-for-agent` label, and it is not a GitHub artifact — only a session can see it.
64	Confirm it exists and that its prompt points at the mounted executor instructions
65	(`.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/executor.md`). Report what you found either way.
66	
67	## 5. End green, or end at `needs-human`
68	
69	Run this repo's checks. Green: push to the branch, then **land the delivery yourself**,
70	per this repo's `maintenance.delivery` in `.claudinite-checks.json`:
71	
72	- **`auto-merge`** — merge the PR. Nothing else will: the deterministic half arms
73	  auto-merge only on a `merge` terminal, and yours was `apply-stage`, so the PR is
74	  sitting unarmed. This is the one step that puts your work on `main`.
75	- **`review`** — leave it open. A human merges it, and that is the setting's whole
76	  meaning.
77	
78	Not green, or a repair you are not sure of: leave the PR open, label
79	it `needs-human`, and say in one comment what is unresolved. A withheld workflow you did
80	not deliver is "not green" — it stays owed, and the next cycle will stage it again.
81	
82	**Why you merge it rather than leaving it.** An unmerged PR is not lost — the next
83	cycle's disposal merges a green one. But `update` is a **daily** task, so "the next
84	cycle" is up to a day away, and until then a workflow you moved into
85	`.github/workflows/` on the branch is not in `.github/workflows/` on `main`. That
86	standing ~24h offset between a run's output and the member's `main` is the exact defect
87	`landDelivery` was written to close for the deterministic half (#649,
88	`engine/scheduler/land-pr.mjs`): *the evidence that settles it does not take a day to
89	arrive*. The same reasoning binds here — the only difference is that you hold the
90	credential, so you are the one who acts on it.
91	
92	Merging is within this task's ceiling (`expected_outcome: 'merged-pr'`), and a ceiling is
93	the most a run may do, never a target — so this is permission, not licence to merge

# Update — the apply stage

The deterministic half already ran. Preprocessing converged this repo's mount to the
canon's current engine and pack versions, ran the version-ranged migrations, gated the
result on the converged tree's own `selftest --strict`, and opened the update PR. The
dispatch issue names the branch and says which packs moved.

**You are here for one of two reasons**, and the issue says which:

- **Withheld workflow files** — content the deterministic half already decided but its
  Action token is refused for. Nothing here needs judgment; you are the credential.
- **A pack's updated rules have met content this repo authored** and the canon has never
  seen. This is the half that needs judgment, and it is all of the judgment there is.

## 1. Read why you are here

The dispatch issue's **Why the agent is here** section names the terminal and the packs
whose versions moved. That is binding scope — do not widen it.

## 2. Deliver any withheld workflow files

GitHub never lets an Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` write under `.github/workflows/`, and the
refusal rejects the whole push — so the update flow stages that content instead of
committing it where it belongs. Anything staged is already on the branch, already in the
PR's diff, and already correct.

If `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` has files in it, then for each one:

- Move it to `.github/workflows/` under the same name — **byte for byte**.
- Delete the staged copy.

Do not reformat it, do not reorder it, do not reconcile it against what the file used to
say. It is a converged artifact, not a draft: the cron minute is a hash of this repo's
full name and the `env:` block is the union of every scheduled task's `required_secrets`,
so an "improvement" here silently changes when this repo runs or which secrets its tasks
can see. A staged file that looks wrong is a `needs-human` end (§5), reported with what
looked wrong — that is a canon bug, and editing it here would hide it while leaving every
other member broken.

An empty or absent `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` means there is nothing owed. Do not
create it, and never move a file INTO it.

## 3. Apply the new rules

Only if the issue's reason names a migration record — it names them by path, e.g.
`packs/basics/migrations/2026-08-13-something`. **Read that record** at
`.claudinite/shared/<path>/migration.mjs`: its `applyStage.instructions` say what its
author wanted done, in their words, and are the specific half of this section. The
record is on the branch you were given because the update that raised it vendored it
there. A record the issue names but the branch does not carry is a `needs-human` end
(§5) — guessing at what its author wanted is worse than reporting it missing.

Then, on that branch:

- Bring this repo's own content in line with the updated pack rules, and repair the
  tests those rules break.
- Nothing outside that scope. No new features, no unrelated tidy-ups, no rewriting a
  member-authored local pack beyond what the new rules require.

## 4. Verify the executor routine

The one check no Action can make. This repo's executor routine fires on the
`ready-for-agent` label, and it is not a GitHub artifact — only a session can see it.
Confirm it exists and that its prompt points at the mounted executor instructions
(`.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/executor.md`). Report what you found either way.

## 5. End green, or end at `needs-human`

Run this repo's checks. Green: push to the branch, then **land the delivery yourself**,
per this repo's `maintenance.delivery` in `.claudinite-checks.json`:

- **`auto-merge`** — merge the PR. Nothing else will: the deterministic half arms
  auto-merge only on a `merge` terminal, and yours was `apply-stage`, so the PR is
  sitting unarmed. This is the one step that puts your work on `main`.
- **`review`** — leave it open. A human merges it, and that is the setting's whole
  meaning.

Not green, or a repair you are not sure of: leave the PR open, label
it `needs-human`, and say in one comment what is unresolved. A withheld workflow you did
not deliver is "not green" — it stays owed, and the next cycle will stage it again.

**Why you merge it rather than leaving it.** An unmerged PR is not lost — the next
cycle's disposal merges a green one. But `update` is a **daily** task, so "the next
cycle" is up to a day away, and until then a workflow you moved into
`.github/workflows/` on the branch is not in `.github/workflows/` on `main`. That
standing ~24h offset between a run's output and the member's `main` is the exact defect
`landDelivery` was written to close for the deterministic half (#649,
`engine/scheduler/land-pr.mjs`): *the evidence that settles it does not take a day to
arrive*. The same reasoning binds here — the only difference is that you hold the
credential, so you are the one who acts on it.

Merging is within this task's ceiling (`expected_outcome: 'merged-pr'`), and a ceiling is
the most a run may do, never a target — so this is permission, not licence to merge
something red. Green first, then merge.

Every non-green end looks the same here, and that is the point — a repair nobody
verified is not a smaller problem than a red check, it is the same problem with less
evidence.

# Claudinite work-item executor (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §6, §10) — a pull worker
# over the queue, triggered by a `task:ready` / `task:urgent` label event for
# latency and by hand for a drain. It carries NO cron: the tick's own drain job is
# the poll that makes a lost label event irrelevant, so events here are latency
# sugar and never the only delivery.
#
# THIS IS THE ONLY PLACE SECRETS LIVE (DESIGN §14). The wiring converge stamps
# every task's declared `required_secrets`, plus each configured invocation
# endpoint's token secret, into the step env below by name — the tick and the
# janitor get none, because they never execute task code. Prework is the only task
# code that ever sees a value; the agent hop carries nothing.
#
# MORE CAPACITY IS MORE EXECUTORS. Nothing enumerates them and each claim is
# independently leased, so a second job, a matrix width, or a runner outside
# Actions entirely all work — the executor's whole interface is issue read/write
# plus the repo at HEAD.
name: Claudinite executor

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  execute:
    # A label event on anything else is not this workflow's business — and a
    # workflow_dispatch carries no label at all, so it always runs.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:ready'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:urgent'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # MUST stay ≤ the engine's executing leash (60m): a hung runner has to be
    # killed by the platform before its claim is reaped and the item re-picked, or
    # a zombie's prework runs beside its replacement's (F17).
    timeout-minutes: 50
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Pick up and execute ready work
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # The wiring converge stamps every declared required_secret, and every
          # configured invocation endpoint's token, below this marker — by name.
          # claudinite:secrets
          CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs

1	// basics task: update — the versioned engine/pack update flows, run by a repo on
2	// itself (#768 — see the versioned-updates design there). The successor to `baselining`,
3	// and for now its sibling: exactly one of the two serves any repo, decided by that
4	// repo's own `maintenance.mechanism` (engine/served-by.mjs).
5	//
6	// A repo that has not been flipped declares nothing, is served by baselining, and
7	// never reaches this task's worker — which stands down in that case rather than
8	// assuming. So adding this task changes nothing for a member until someone writes
9	// the flag into its declaration.
10	//
11	// Two stages, like baselining's. The DETERMINISTIC flows are `prework`
12	// (worker.mjs): they converge the mount, run the version-ranged migrations, gate on
13	// the converged tree's self-test, open the PR, and act on the terminal. The AGENT
14	// stage runs only when the pack flow's apply stage is needed — the pack's new rules
15	// meeting member-authored content the canon has never seen.
16	//
17	// Self-contained (imports nothing) so the scheduler, executor, and a human all load
18	// it standalone — the whole contract lives in this default export.
19	
20	const OVERDUE_DAYS = 1;
21	
22	export default {
23	  id: 'update',
24	  frequency: 'daily-2h',                 // the same 02:00 slot baselining holds: a repo's mount is converged before anything reads it
25	  precondition_signals: ['stamp', 'sharedMount'],
26	  agent_model: 'sonnet',                 // the apply stage only — most runs are agentless
27	  expected_outcome: 'merged-pr',
28	  agent_instructions: 'task.md',
29	
30	  prework: 'node worker.mjs',
31	  prework_timeout: 900,
32	  agent_execution_timeout: 1800,
33	
34	  // PURE over the collected signals. It gates only that the worker RUNS; the worker
35	  // owns every decision after that, including whether this repo is its to serve —
36	  // which is deliberately NOT decided here. The signals carry the stamp, not the
37	  // declaration, and a precondition that guessed at the mechanism from a stamp would
38	  // be a second answer to a question `servedBy` already answers from the file.
39	  precondition(signals) {
40	    const stamp = signals.stamp ?? {};
41	    if (!stamp.ref && stamp.ageDays === null) {
42	      return { run: false, reason: 'no vendored mount (no stamp) — nothing to update' };
43	    }
44	    const age = stamp.ageDays;
45	    if (age !== null && age < OVERDUE_DAYS && !(signals.sharedMount?.changedPacks ?? []).length) {
46	      return { run: false, reason: `converged ${age}d ago and no pack moved — nothing due` };
47	    }
48	    return {
49	      run: true,
50	      reason: 'the mount is due an update pass',
51	      context: [
52	        'The deterministic flows have already run: the mount is converged, the version-ranged migrations applied, and the update PR is open.',
53	        'Your job is only the apply stage — bring this repo\'s own content in line with the updated pack rules on that branch, and verify the executor routine. Do not re-run the mechanical converge.',
54	      ],
55	    };
56	  },
57	};

18	// names no longer exists, so a repo declaring it gets NOTHING and must be told so
19	// loudly rather than served silently.
20	//
21	// The default is a READING, not a policy. The corpus's rule is that automation
22	// maintains the explicit value in every file it maintains, so the flag sits visibly
23	// in the exact file anyone would go to change it, and a missing key becomes drift the
24	// automation repairs rather than a case code must interpret forever. `servedBy`
25	// therefore reports whether the value was DECLARED or inferred.
26	// THE NAME IS `versioned`, and `updates` is its own legacy alias.
27	//
28	// The mechanism and the TASK that runs it had names one letter apart — mechanism
29	// `updates`, task `update` — which is not a style complaint: the two appear together
30	// in the same sentences, in `FORCE_TASKS=update` beside `mechanism: "updates"`, and a
31	// reader with no way to tell which noun they are looking at will eventually type the
32	// wrong one. The mechanism is renamed rather than the task because the mechanism is
33	// what the design already calls this thing everywhere else — "versioned updates"
34	// (docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md) — while `update` is the right name for a task,
35	// which is an action a repo performs.
36	//
37	// `updates` STAYS RECOGNISED for the same reason `baselining` does, and for a
38	// narrower window: it is stamped in every member's declaration right now, and a
39	// member reads its own declaration with the engine it currently has, which is one
40	// cycle behind the record that renames it. A member converging mid-rename must not
41	// find its own mechanism unrecognised — that reads as `invalid`, which resolves to
42	// the default with the offending value attached, and would make a correctly-declared
43	// repo look misdeclared for exactly one cycle. The `basics` record retires it from
44	// declarations; this list retires it from the vocabulary a release later.
45	export const MECHANISMS = ['baselining', 'updates', 'versioned'];
46	export const DEFAULT_MECHANISM = 'versioned';
47	
48	// The mechanism that no longer exists — kept nameable so the one caller that must
49	// explain the dead end can name it without hard-coding the string.
50	export const RETIRED_MECHANISM = 'baselining';
51	
52	// …and the one being renamed out of declarations, still fully served while members
53	// carry it. Distinct from RETIRED: a repo declaring this gets maintained normally,
54	// it is simply spelled the old way.
55	export const LEGACY_MECHANISM = 'updates';
56	export const VERSIONED_MECHANISM = 'versioned';
57	
58	// The declaration key. Beside `delivery`, because both answer "how is this repo
59	// maintained" and a second home for the same question is how a repo ends up
60	// answering it twice, differently.
61	export const MAINTENANCE = 'maintenance';
62	export const MECHANISM_KEY = 'mechanism';
63	
64	// `{ mechanism, declared }` — the mechanism to run, and whether the repo actually
65	// said so. An unrecognised value is NOT silently treated as the default: it is the
66	// one case where guessing could hand a repo to the wrong mechanism, so it reports
67	// itself as undeclared with the offending value attached, and a caller that cares
68	// stops rather than picking.
69	export function servedBy(declaration) {
70	  const raw = declaration?.[MAINTENANCE]?.[MECHANISM_KEY];
71	  if (raw === undefined || raw === null) return { mechanism: DEFAULT_MECHANISM, declared: false };
72	  if (typeof raw !== 'string' || !MECHANISMS.includes(raw)) {
73	    return { mechanism: DEFAULT_MECHANISM, declared: false, invalid: raw };
74	  }
75	  return { mechanism: raw, declared: true };
76	}
77	
78	// The two questions the mechanisms ask about themselves, so neither has to know the
79	// other's name at its call site — and so the "exactly one" property is one
80	// expression rather than two that can disagree.
81	// Both spellings answer yes: a member on the old name is served by the same flows,
82	// so every caller asking "are the update flows mine to run" gets one answer whichever
83	// word the repo happens to carry this cycle.
84	export const servedByUpdates = (declaration) =>
85	  [LEGACY_MECHANISM, VERSIONED_MECHANISM].includes(servedBy(declaration).mechanism);
86	export const servedByBaselining = (declaration) => servedBy(declaration).mechanism === RETIRED_MECHANISM;
87	
88	// The declaration a flip writes: the mechanism made explicit, everything else
89	// untouched. Returned rather than written, so the caller that owns the file owns the
90	// write — and so this stays testable without one.
91	export function withMechanism(declaration, mechanism) {
92	  if (!MECHANISMS.includes(mechanism)) throw new Error(`unknown mechanism "${mechanism}" — one of ${MECHANISMS.join(', ')}`);
93	  const base = declaration && typeof declaration === 'object' && !Array.isArray(declaration) ? declaration : {};
94	  return { ...base, [MAINTENANCE]: { ...(base[MAINTENANCE] ?? {}), [MECHANISM_KEY]: mechanism } };
95	}
